scope: Duddingston’s Robert: the Corsoun household as preferred uncertain parents

working_parent_replacements.basis: The preferred local working parents of the Duddingston Robert are now Andrew Glasgow and Elizat Stevinsoun, through possible identity with their recorded son Robert-4006. The accepted 1597/8 testament expressly names Robert as Andrew’s son by Elizat and makes provision until he reached age. A minor then can fit the adult generation of the Robert buried at Duddingston in 1647 and the probable father of James the Edinburgh weaver. The retained circa-1582 and 1597/before-1597 dates are estimates or bounds, not two exact birth records in conflict. On the maintained, queried Calder-area reading of Andrew’s residence, this offers a positive named-child family candidate in the relevant broad Lothian comparison. The earlier Archibald/Isobell pair has no record naming the Duddingston Robert as its child. Prefer the recorded Corsoun family as the uncertain route, with both former parents retained as alternatives.
working_parent_replacements.limitations: The 1598 child and the Duddingston adult remain separate WikiTree profiles with an uncertain identity comparison; no merge is inferred. No holding, occupation, wife or named-relative bridge equates them, and the Corsoun/Calder place reading itself remains queried. A different local Robert, including the separate Ninian-son account Robert-1027, remains a comparison. Ninian’s son keeps his proved parents and is not conflated with Andrew’s named son. Elizat’s maternity is direct for the recorded child only; it is uncertain for the Duddingston adult because it depends on the same identity hypothesis. Archibald’s and Isobell’s biological parentage is not disproved. James-1150’s probable father assessment, all other selected families, and the adult’s existing vital fields remain unchanged. Two modern Robert accounts can represent one historical son; they are not independent evidence for two sons.
